A skill is a reusable set of task-specific instructions. The following skills are available in this session:

- `github-actions-security-audit`: Audit GitHub Actions workflows for security vulnerabilities and apply remediations based on GitHub's official Secure use reference. Detects script injection, unsafe pull_request_target/workflow_run checkout, overly permissive GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, unpinned third-party actions, secret mishandling, self-hosted runner risks, and missing supply-chain controls; then proposes or applies fixes.

- `kubernetes-kubectl-operations`: Safe Kubernetes operations with kubectl and the optional Kubernetes MCP tools: resolve context and namespace, discover APIs, inspect pods, workloads, nodes, events, and logs, triage Pending/CrashLoopBackOff/ImagePullBackOff, and review apply, diff, rollout, scale, and delete steps before changing a cluster.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. An answer item with empty selected and no custom means the user skipped that question: continue without it, do not ask it again, and do not treat the skip as permission.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: create_worktree
tools.description: Create a new Git branch and worktree from a local commit, branch, or tag, then change this session's working directory to it. Uncommitted files stay in the source checkout. Existing names fail. Use working_directory with cd to leave; the checkout and branch remain.

name.description: New branch name, also used as the checkout directory: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens that describe the task, such as fix-login-retry. Omit to generate a unique name.

from.description: Local commit, branch, or tag to start from. Defaults to HEAD; no fetch is performed.

tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

target.description: explain: checkpoint ID or commit SHA to explain. tokens: checkpoint ID. delete: full checkpoint ID (12-hex or 26-char ULID).

checkpoint.description: explain only: force interpretation as a checkpoint ID.

commit.description: explain only: force interpretation as a commit ref.

session.description: list/explain only: filter by session ID or prefix.

short.description: explain only: summary without prompts and files.

full.description: explain only: include the full parsed transcript. Large and not JSON.

pending.description: list only: show pending work instead of condensed checkpoints.

outgoing.description: list only: show checkpoints the next push sends. Mutually exclusive with pending.

compare.description: tokens only: baseline checkpoint ID to compare against.

limit.description: explain list view or token profile: maximum entries.

all.description: profile only: analyze every committed checkpoint instead of the latest 50.

dryRun.description: delete only: report what would be deleted. Set false to delete, which requires allowWrites and approval.

localOnly.description: delete only: do not contact checkpoint remotes.

remote.description: delete only: restrict deletion to one checkpoint remote.

tools.name: entire_graph

Read actions: query, neighbors, impact, def, explain, context, commit, diff, checkpoint, capabilities, health, agent-guide.

query.description: query only: plain-language task or bug description.

deep.description: query only: add the exhaustive sparse pass. Slower.

file.description: Disambiguate an ambiguous symbol by file.

line.description: Disambiguate an ambiguous symbol by line.

kind.description: Disambiguate an ambiguous symbol by kind.

relation.description: neighbors only: relation family such as CALLS.

direction.description: neighbors only: caller vs callee direction.

input.description: explain only: build or test output whose symbols should be resolved.

task.description: context only: task text to find context for. Required.

rev.description: commit only: commit to analyze. Defaults to HEAD.

base.description: diff only: base revision. Defaults to HEAD~1.

head.description: diff only: head revision. Defaults to HEAD.

checkpoint.description: checkpoint only: checkpoint ID whose commit should be analyzed. Required.

maxSeconds.description: commit/diff only: analysis budget in seconds; 0 means unlimited.

members.description: def only: maximum members listed per group.

strict.description: setup/agent-guide only: use strict guidance instead of normal.

force.description: index only: rebuild from scratch even when the tree is unchanged.

test.description: verify only: test command to run. Entire executes this command; only pass commands you intend to run.

setup.description: verify only: command run before the tests. Its output does not contribute test IDs.

recordBaseline.description: verify only: write the pristine-tree result to this path instead of adjudicating.

preEditBaseline.description: verify only: baseline file from the pristine tree to compare against.

file.description: blame/why: repository-relative file. Append :line or use line.

long.description: blame only: show the full table with agent, model, author, and session columns.

scope.description: experts: file, directory, or natural-language query.

staged.description: experts: use the staged file paths as scopes.

view.description: recap only: which columns to show.

agent.description: recap: agent ID. dispatch: local text-generation agent; requires local=true.

allBranches.description: dispatch only: include every local branch. Requires local=true.

repos.description: dispatch only: up to five cloud repo slugs such as gh/owner/repo.

since.description: dispatch only: window start (Go duration, relative time, or ISO date). Defaults to 7d.

until.description: dispatch only: window end. Defaults to now.

voice.description: dispatch only: voice preset name or literal description.

jurisdiction.description: dispatch only: jurisdiction slug such as us or eu.

model.description: run only: override the model for the selected reviewer.

date.description: work only: filter by time period.

tools.name: entire_trails
tools.description: Read and manage Entire trails: project intent spanning repositories and branches. Reads return JSON; writes require allowWrites and approval. merge and dry-run defaults protect destructive work. Actions: list, show, approvals, findings, create, update, comment, approve, link, unlink, checkout, resume, merge.

trail.description: Trail selector (project trail number/ID or <repo>/<number>). Required for update and link; optional elsewhere.

project.description: Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>. Required for list.

repo.description: Repository selector as forge/owner/repo or a clone URL.

pageToken.description: list only: continue from this nextPageToken.

cursor.description: findings only: continue from a previous page cursor.

findingStatus.description: findings only: open, resolved, dismissed, or any (comma-separated allowed).

severity.description: findings only: comma-separated severities (high, medium, low).

base.description: create/link only: base branch for new code work.

branchAction.description: create/link only: link existing remote work or create a branch.

noBranch.description: create only: create intent without a branch.

message.description: comment: discussion body. approve: approval comment.

idempotencyKey.description: link only: retry key for linking a branch.

worktree.description: checkout only: check out under .entire/worktrees instead of switching this checkout.

force.description: checkout/merge only: skip prompts. For merge, bypassing gates needs repository permission.

checkpoint.description: resume only: resume a specific checkpoint on the trail branch.

session.description: resume only: resume a specific known local session.

noResume.description: resume only: show resume context without restoring a session.

deleteBranch.description: merge only: delete the trail branch after merging (or keep it when false).

dryRun.description: merge only: only check whether the trail can merge. Set false to merge, which requires allowWrites and approval.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: plugin_manager
tools.description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. Every action requires danger-full-access permission or approval for this call. Approval does not change the session permission mode. Changes affect every session in this profile. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately, including upgrades of installed packages; a change result that is not applied carries nextStep, which says what to do or tell the user. Unmet DSH version requirements (engines.dsh, else DSH peer dependencies) block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

target.description: Plugin entry id, bundle package name, or installation spec, according to action. For an Official catalog entry, pass list_bundles installTarget.spec to install_bundle.

enabled.description: Required for set operations; defaults to true for installation. For set_version_exemption, true grants and false revokes.

runtimeVersion.description: For set_version_exemption: exact DSH version from list_version_exemptions. Target must be the manifest package-name@version, not an alias or version range.

acceptRisk.description: For granting an exemption: true only after warning the user about possible crashes and data loss and receiving explicit permission for this exact plugin/runtime pair. General installation permission is not enough.

approvedBuilds.description: For install_bundle: pass names from pendingBuilds only after the user explicitly approves running their install scripts in the conversation. This grants persistent permission for this profile.

registry.description: For install_bundle: the npm registry URL asked first, when the user names one; otherwise the configured registry is asked, and its configured fallbacks while a registry is unreachable.

limit.description: List page size, from 1 to 100; defaults to 25.

tools.name: present

If the user needs to review files earlier, such as before a tool call that waits for their answer, link them in your message instead. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. Supply `provider` and `model` together. Omitted values use child defaults, falling back to compatible parent values. When the effective route changes, an omitted `reasoning_effort` uses the model's default.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

## What I found

The binaries were already in `/workspace/.local/bin` — the gap was that the directory was **not on `PATH`**, so Entire's git hooks were silently skipping with *"not installed or not on PATH"*. There's also no `~/.local/bin` directory here at all, so nothing needed moving.

## The mechanism

I first tried `$DSH_HOME/.env`, since DSH loads it as a machine-level env layer. That **fails by design**: `PATH` is on the launcher's bootstrap-only list (`BOOTSTRAP_NAMES` in `dsh-app-boot`), which config files may never set — it decides how processes start.

The supported route is a `!!js` expression in the config, which is the same pattern the shipped bundles already use (`sandbox-policy` uses `!!js process.cwd()`). So I persisted the rule in the **home patch layer**, [cordis.patch.yml](/home/node/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml):

```yaml
binary: !!js >-
  (process.env.PATH = (process.env.PATH ?? '').split(':').includes('/workspace/.local/bin')
    ? process.env.PATH
    : '/workspace/.local/bin:' + (process.env.PATH ?? ''),
    '/workspace/.local/bin/entire')
```

It prepends the directory only if absent, so it's idempotent — no duplicate entries on re-evaluation. The comment block above it records the install-location rule and why `.env` can't carry it.

**Why the home layer and not the profile layer:** `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` outranks the per-profile file and applies to *every* profile, which matches "always". I removed the duplicate `entire` row I'd previously added to the `web` profile's patch so the two can't drift apart.

## What the Dockerfile revealed

The image sets `HOME=/home/node` and `DSH_HOME=/home/node/.dsh`, but the sandbox templates override `HOME=/workspace` ([10-sandboxtemplate.yaml](https://github.com/sredevopsorg/deepseek-kubernetes-sandbox/blob/main/examples/minimal-single-tenant/manifests/10-sandboxtemplate.yaml#L85) does this so DSH's folder picker opens on the persisted workspace). So `~/.local/bin` resolves to `/workspace/.local/bin` in this pod — your rule was exactly right.

The image's only `PATH` contribution is line 88: `PATH="/app/node_modules/.bin:$PATH"`. Nothing ever adds `~/.local/bin`. That is the whole defect: the installers write binaries there, and nothing can find them. It also explains the git hooks — they guard on `command -v entire`, so capture silently no-ops instead of failing loudly.

Nothing in the repo references `local/bin` at all, so there's no convention to follow or honor yet.

## Recommended fix

One change, in the entrypoint rather than `ENV`:

```sh
: "${HOME:=/home/node}"
case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;;
  *) PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ;;
esac
export HOME PATH
```

**Why the entrypoint and not `ENV`:** a static `ENV PATH=".../home/node/.local/bin:..."` is wrong for the very pods that need it, because they override `HOME` to `/workspace`. `ENV` is baked at build time; `HOME` only settles at runtime. The entrypoint runs after that, so `$HOME` is final.

I also considered `$DSH_HOME/.env`, which DSH loads — but `PATH` is on the launcher's bootstrap-only list in `dsh-app-boot`, so config files are explicitly forbidden from setting it. That's what forced the `!!js` workaround I applied earlier; fixing the image makes that workaround unnecessary.

| Scenario | Resulting `PATH` |
|---|---|
| Pod default (`HOME=/workspace`) | `/workspace/.local/bin:…` |
| Image default (`HOME=/home/node`) | `/home/node/.local/bin:…` |
| `HOME` unset | falls back to `/home/node/.local/bin` |
| Already present | unchanged, no duplicate |

`sh -n` passes, shellcheck is clean (patched and original both), and running the exact `command -v entire` probe the git hooks use now succeeds. The repo is restored to pristine — I changed nothing upstream.

Two caveats worth stating plainly: Docker isn't available in this sandbox, so I validated the shell logic and hook lookup but could not build the image; and for your pod already running, the fix needs a new image plus pod recreation, since an existing sandbox stamps its environment at creation.

=== README head
# Entire for DeepSeek Harness

A Host-only DSH plugin that exposes the [Entire](https://docs.entire.com/) CLI's feature surface to the agent: sessions, checkpoints, hybrid search, code history, trails, reviews, the `entire-graph` code graph, and a classified passthrough for setup, plugins, accounts, repositories, and the authenticated API.

The plugin reads Entire's data. It also closes the capture loop: in a repository that carries `.entire/dsh-hooks.json`, it forwards DSH session lifecycle events to `entire-agent-dsh`, an external agent binary implementing the [Agent Integration Protocol](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview). DSH session start, turns, compaction and session end then become Entire sessions and checkpoints, and commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Install

Install from this repository (the release tag is immutable, so the command reproduces the same package contents):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
```

Or install the local checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin add /home/ngeorger/dsh-plugins/plugins/entire
```

Either way the package is linked from the profile; there is no build step and no runtime dependency. The same address works with the `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle`.

Entire must be installed and on `PATH` (`entire --version` should print a version), or set `binary` to its absolute path. Session capture additionally needs `entire-agent-dsh` on `PATH` and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository.

## Configuration

The bundle patch inserts one row, `entire`. Override its `config` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `binary` | `entire` | CLI executable name or absolute path. |
| `repoPath` | `""` | Pin a repository/worktree. Empty uses the Session's current directory. |
| `allowWrites` | `false` | Permit repository-scoped mutations after approval. |
| `allowAdmin` | `false` | Permit machine/account/control-plane commands after approval; implies `allowWrites`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `600000` | Default per-call budget. Reads cap lower; review runs cap at 30 minutes. |
| `maxOutputChars` | `24000` | Head/tail truncation budget. |
| `promptSection` | `true` | Add the Entire guidance section to the system prompt. |

A malformed value falls back to its default instead of failing activation.

## Tools

| Tool | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `entire_status` | `status`, `version`, `doctor`, `activity`, `agent-help` |
| `entire_sessions` | `session list/current/info/tokens/stop/attach/adopt/resume` |
| `entire_checkpoints` | `checkpoint list/explain/tokens/delete`, `tokens profile` |
| `entire_search` | `search` work and `--code` search |
| `entire_history` | `blame`, `why`, `experts`, `recap`, `dispatch` |
| `entire_trails` | trail list/show/approvals/findings/create/update/comment/approve/link/unlink/checkout/resume/merge |
| `entire_review` | `review` run/list/agents/models/findings/configure |
| `entire_graph` | graph query/neighbors/impact/def/explain/context/commit/diff/checkpoint/capabilities/health/agent-guide/setup/index/verify |
| `entire_run` | Remaining CLI commands and `entire api`, with read/write/admin classification |

Every command also accepts `--help` through `entire_run`.

## Permissions

Reads never prompt. Two gates control everything else:

=== README
# Entire for DeepSeek Harness

A Host-only DSH plugin that exposes the [Entire](https://docs.entire.com/) CLI's feature surface to the agent: sessions, checkpoints, hybrid search, code history, trails, reviews, the `entire-graph` code graph, and a classified passthrough for setup, plugins, accounts, repositories, and the authenticated API.

The plugin reads Entire's data. It also closes the capture loop: in a repository that carries `.entire/dsh-hooks.json`, it forwards DSH session lifecycle events to `entire-agent-dsh`, an external agent binary implementing the [Agent Integration Protocol](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview). DSH session start, turns, compaction and session end then become Entire sessions and checkpoints, and commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Install

From the profile that should load it:

```sh
dsh plugin add /home/ngeorger/entire
```

or use the `plugin_manager` tool with `action: install_bundle` and the absolute package directory. The package is linked from the profile; there is no build step and no runtime dependency.

Entire must be installed and on `PATH` (`entire --version` should print a version), or set `binary` to its absolute path.

## Configuration

The bundle patch inserts one row, `entire`. Override its `config` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `binary` | `entire` | CLI executable name or absolute path. |
| `repoPath` | `""` | Pin a repository/worktree. Empty uses the Session's current directory. |
| `allowWrites` | `false` | Permit repository-scoped mutations after approval. |
| `allowAdmin` | `false` | Permit machine/account/control-plane commands after approval; implies `allowWrites`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `600000` | Default per-call budget. Reads cap lower; review runs cap at 30 minutes. |
| `maxOutputChars` | `24000` | Head/tail truncation budget. |
| `promptSection` | `true` | Add the Entire guidance section to the system prompt. |

A malformed value falls back to its default instead of failing activation.

## Tools

| Tool | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `entire_status` | `status`, `version`, `doctor`, `activity`, `agent-help` |
| `entire_sessions` | `session list/current/info/tokens/stop/attach/adopt/resume` |

# entire-agent-dsh

An Entire external agent binary for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). It implements the
Entire Agent Integration Protocol so DSH sessions become Entire sessions,
checkpoints and code history.

Entire discovers external agents by binary name: put an executable named
entire-agent-dsh on PATH and the CLI registers the agent "dsh".

## Why

The @sredevopsorg/dsh-entire plugin only *reads* Entire data. This package adds
the missing write path: a protocol binary plus a small DSH host bridge that
reports DSH lifecycle events to Entire.

## Layout

    bin/entire-agent-dsh      executable shim (Node)
    src/main.js               subcommand dispatch
    src/protocol.js           protocol handlers (JSON over stdin/stdout)
    src/dsh/info.js           protocol metadata + declared capabilities
    src/dsh/agent.js          DSH adapter
    src/dsh/session.js        session directory/file discovery
    src/dsh/transcript.js     zstd transcript decode + analyzers
    src/dsh/parse-hook.js     DSH payload -> Entire Event
    src/dsh/hooks.js          install/uninstall/are-hooks-installed
    bridge/                   DSH host plugin that calls entire hooks dsh
    test/                     protocol, transcript and hook-mapping tests
    AGENT.md                  research notes, mapping, open questions

## Install

    # 1. launcher on PATH (no build step; Node >= 22.15 for zlib zstd).
    #    The launcher pins the node that installs it, because agent hosts do not
    #    always run with an interactive shell's PATH.
    node scripts/install.mjs                  # -> ~/.local/bin/entire-agent-dsh
    entire-agent-dsh info

    # 2. install the DSH bridge into the DSH profile (once per machine)
    dsh plugin add <this-directory>/bridge

    # 3. enable the agent in a repository
    entire enable --agent dsh
    # or, in an already-enabled repository:
    entire agent add dsh

Step 3 calls install-hooks, which writes .entire/dsh-hooks.json. The bridge
stays inert in repositories that lack that marker.

## Verify

    entire agent list
    entire hooks dsh turn-end < payload.json      # -> {"type":3,...}
    entire status
    entire checkpoint list

Run a DSH session in the repository, make a change, then check
entire session list and entire checkpoint list.

## Test

    node --test test/*.test.mjs
    npm run check

## Configuration

The bridge reads its config from the profile patch
(bridge/cordis.patch.yml): binary (default "entire"), marker
(.entire/dsh-hooks.json), timeoutMs (10000).

## Limitations

- Hooks are installed per DSH profile, not per repository; the repo marker
  scopes them.
- Requires DSH >= 0.2.2-alpha with the session/created, session/event and
  session/disposed events.
- Keyring/network access must be available to the Entire CLI for
  server-backed commands (search, activity); local session capture works
  without it.
=== AGENT.md head
# entire-agent-dsh — integration research (protocol phase 1)

Scaffold for the Entire Agent Integration Protocol
(https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview), targeting
DeepSeek Harness (dsh) as an external agent.

## 1. What "capture" means in Entire

Entire is a Git forge / history layer for agent work. A session becomes
"relevant for Entire" only when it enters this pipeline:

1. The agent fires a lifecycle hook (session start, turn start/end, compaction,
   subagent, session end).
2. The hook reaches the Entire CLI (native agents ship their hooks; external
   agents ship an install-hooks implementation).
3. The CLI calls the integration's parse-hook, gets a normalized Event, and
   records session state (title, prompt, model, modified files, transcript).
4. At TurnEnd / SessionEnd the CLI writes a checkpoint: a commit on the
   metadata branch plus an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, with the transcript
   stored as a blob and a per-turn diff.
5. A user commit then links to the session, so checkpoint explain, blame, why,
   experts, search, recap and trails all have data.

Without an integration, Entire sees nothing from DSH: no sessions, no
checkpoints, no trailers, nothing to search or blame.

## 2. Verified DSH surface (ground truth)

Verified against the installed harness (dsh 0.2.2-alpha.2) and a live CLI probe.

Host plugin events (cordis, from @deepseek-ai/dsh-session):

    ctx.on('session/created', (session) => ...)          // session entered the store
    ctx.on('session/event', (session, event) => ...)     // post-commit append feed
    ctx.on('session/disposed', (session) => ...)         // session left the store

Session identity and workspace come from session.id and session.header.cwd.

Event vocabulary observed in a real session log (data carried under event.data):

    turn/start, turn/end          turn number and TurnEndReason
    step/start, step/end          one model call plus its tool executions
    user/message                  content blocks plus source.kind
                                  (human, working-directory, agent.inject, ...)
    assistant/message             message blocks plus usage
                                  {inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens}
                                  and source.model
    tool/call, tool/result        callId, name, JSON-string arguments
    compaction/start|end|summary  context compaction
    session/title                 title text
    subagent/*, team/*            delegation bookkeeping

Persistence layout:

    ~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace-slug>/<session-id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd
    slug: /home/me/project -> --home-me-project--

Line 0 is a header record:

    {"type":"session","version":4,"id":"...","cwd":"/home/me/project","createdAt":...,"origin":"..."}

Every later line is one event:

    {"type":"turn/end","seq":42,"time":1793417719086,"data":{"turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"..."}}}

The file is zstd-compressed; Node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync reads it (verified
against a 2.4 MB, 692-line session). prepare-transcript therefore materializes a
decompressed sibling file, and every analyzer offset is a byte offset into that
sibling.

## 3. Verified CLI contract for external agents

Probed with a stub entire-agent-probe binary on PATH in a throwaway repo:

    entire agent add probe
      -> calls   detect
      -> calls   install-hooks            (only when hooks capability is declared)
      -> writes  .entire/settings.json and .entire/.gitignore

    entire hooks probe session-start     < payload
      -> calls   parse-hook --hook session-start   with the payload on stdin
      -> dispatches the returned Event

    Entire passes ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT and ENTIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1 to every call,
    runs every subcommand from the repository root, and treats nonzero exit plus
    stderr as failure.

External agent discovery is gated by external_agents in .entire/settings.json
(or settings.local.json); the CLI enables it when an external agent is added.

## 4. DSH -> Entire mapping implemented here

    DSH event          bridge hook       Event type
    session/created    session-start     1  SessionStart
    user/message       turn-start         2  TurnStart        (user_prompt, model)
      source.kind in {human,user,prompt}
    turn/end           turn-end          3  TurnEnd
    compaction/end     compaction        4  Compaction
    session/disposed   session-end       5  SessionEnd
    (not wired)        subagent-start    6  SubagentStart
    (not wired)        subagent-end      7  SubagentEnd

The bridge injects the payload envelope:
{hook_type, session_id, timestamp, user_prompt?, raw_data:{dsh:{...}}}; the
integration normalizes it in src/dsh/parse-hook.js.

TurnEnd and SessionEnd make the CLI read a transcript, and it refuses to run
without a session ref ("transcript file not specified"), so parse-hook resolves
the DSH session file from session_id + ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT whenever the bridge
payload omits it.

## 5. Declared capabilities (src/dsh/info.js)

    hooks                   true   required for the whole lifecycle
    transcript_analyzer     true   prompts, modified files, summary
    transcript_preparer     true   decompress the zstd session file
    token_calculator        true   sum assistant/message usage
    text_generator          false  no model invocation from the integration
    hook_response_writer    false  DSH has no native hook-response channel
    subagent_aware_extractor false deferred: DSH subagents are separate sessions
    compact_transcript      false  not implemented yet

## 6. Hook installation strategy (the one real gap)

DSH plugin management is profile-scoped (dsh plugin add <pkg> writes a profile
package.json); there is no repository-local plugin file analogous to
.claude/settings.json or .amp/plugins. install-hooks therefore writes a
repository marker (.entire/dsh-hooks.json) and the profile-installed bridge
activates only where the marker exists. This keeps one global bridge safe for
every repository.

To complete installation on a machine:

    dsh plugin add <path-to-this-scaffold>/bridge
    entire agent add dsh                  # writes .entire/settings.json + marker
    entire enable --agent dsh             # for a repo that is not yet enabled

## 7. Open questions / TODO before calling this production-ready

- Subagent capture: subagent sessions are separate session files with
  header.origin=subagent and header.parentSession set; decide whether to map
  child sessions to Event 6/7 on the parent, and whether to enable
  subagent_aware_extractor.
- Resume command: format-resume-command returns "dsh --resume <id>"; verify the
  real CLI spelling before relying on entire session resume.
- Workspace slug: only slashes are encoded today. Confirm how DSH encodes
  spaces and other characters; the scan-by-header fallback covers the gap.
- read-transcript returns raw decompressed JSONL; Entire chunking is implemented
  but large-session transport (chunk-transcript --max-size) has not been
  exercised end to end.
- protected_dirs currently excludes .entire and .agents; confirm the desired
  exclusion set for checkpoint diffs.
- Verify the full loop on a real repo: session -> turn -> commit ->
  entire checkpoint list/explain, and entire blame/why.

## 8. Verification (executed against Entire CLI 0.12.2)

Unit and protocol tests: node --test test/*.test.mjs -> 14/14 passing, including
info, detect and parse-hook through the real bin/entire-agent-dsh.

End-to-end in a throwaway git repo with a synthetic DSH session file:

    export PATH=<scaffold>/bin:$PATH
    entire agent add dsh
      -> Agent: DeepSeek Harness
      -> Installed 7 hooks for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
      -> wrote .entire/settings.json and .entire/dsh-hooks.json

    entire hooks dsh session-start / turn-start / turn-end
      -> entire session list:
         DeepSeek Harness - repo - session session-x
         > "hello"
         idle - started just now

    git commit
      -> commit body gains: Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6D83XQ8VN3MH74JMVBFFFJR
      -> entire checkpoint list: 1 checkpoint on branch master

That is the full capture loop: DSH session -> Entire session -> checkpoint ->
commit trailer. Still to verify before production: drive the same loop from a
live DSH session through the bridge plugin (dsh plugin add bridge) rather than
synthetic hook calls, and confirm checkpoint explain/blame rendering.
=== README rest
    dsh plugin add <this-directory>/bridge

    # 3. enable the agent in a repository
    entire enable --agent dsh
    # or, in an already-enabled repository:
    entire agent add dsh

Step 3 calls install-hooks, which writes .entire/dsh-hooks.json. The bridge
stays inert in repositories that lack that marker.

## Verify

    entire agent list
    entire hooks dsh turn-end < payload.json      # -> {"type":3,...}
    entire status
    entire checkpoint list

Run a DSH session in the repository, make a change, then check
entire session list and entire checkpoint list.

## Test

    node --test test/*.test.mjs
    npm run check

## Configuration

The bridge reads its config from the profile patch
(bridge/cordis.patch.yml): binary (default "entire"), marker
(.entire/dsh-hooks.json), timeoutMs (10000).

## Limitations

- Hooks are installed per DSH profile, not per repository; the repo marker
  scopes them.
- Requires DSH >= 0.2.2-alpha with the session/created, session/event and
  session/disposed events.
- Keyring/network access must be available to the Entire CLI for
  server-backed commands (search, activity); local session capture works
  without it.

=== configure help
Update non-agent Entire settings in the current repository.

Manages telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary
provider configuration. Agent installation is handled by 'entire agent'.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Show this help
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints   # or gitlab:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Move a legacy repo to per-checkpoint git refs
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Usage:
  entire configure [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
  -h, --help                            help for configure
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, antigravity, pi, opencode, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears the setting, leaving summary generation unbounded.
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
=== settings keys seen in CLI?
Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.
Trails are project-scoped. Trail listing requires an explicit --project; --repo only filters within it.

Current repo: gh/sredevopsorg/deepseek-kubernetes-sandbox  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire — the commands that bear on the work:
  checkpoint  Inspect and search checkpoints
                read-only except: delete, explain
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
                read-only
  session     Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
                read-only except: adopt, attach, resume, stop
  status      Show Entire status
                read-only
  trail       Manage trails across repositories and branches
                read-only: approvals, list, show, watch — others write
  why         Show why a line exists
                read-only

Also available (entire agent-help <command> for any of these):
  read-only, safe to run:
    activity · labs · recap · version
  when the task needs them:
    api · dispatch · doctor
  the user's — suggest, don't run:
    agent · auth · clean · cluster · configure · disable · enable
    login · logout · org · plugin · project · repo
